_comment: Recall-quality fixture v2 (HGT-22). Stress-tests the §9 categories the private eval explicitly names — multi-hop linkage, keyword-anchored retrieval, supersession arcs (opinion + employment), noise resistance, implicit facts — plus tight-budget priority assembly probes that prove HGT-19 facts-first ordering is query-aware (not 'dump everything'). Every user_id starts with 'fix-' so /admin/run_fixture can reset safely.
name: recall-v2

conversations._purpose: Multi-hop probe: pet name in one turn, city in another. Expected: Known facts block fuses both.

messages.content: Just got my dog Biscuit yesterday — he's a beagle, three years old.
Welcome to the family, Biscuit!
Loving Berlin so far, moved here from NYC last month.
Berlin is a great city. How are you settling in?

conversations._purpose: Keyword-anchored vs distractor-paraphrase: probe `Stripe` should pick the literal-token turn even though the distractor is semantically richer.

messages.content: Left Stripe last month after four years there.
Big change. What's next?
My old company was very large and well-known, I worked there for years before joining a smaller startup. I miss the scale of the engineering teams there but the small team is more fun.
That's a familiar trade-off.

conversations._purpose: Ten facts on one user. Tight-budget probes should surface query-relevant facts only. Today this fails (HGT-19 is type-priority sorted, not query-aware) — that failure is HGT-23's acceptance metric.

messages.content: I work at Notion as a product manager.
Cool.
I live in Berlin, moved from NYC last year.
Nice.
I have a cat named Mochi.
Sweet name.
Also have a dog named Biscuit, a three-year-old beagle.
Two pets!
I'm vegetarian and allergic to shellfish. Also I don't drink coffee.
Noted.
Honestly I think TypeScript generics are over-engineered.
A common take.

conversations._purpose: Supersession arc on opinion. Three statements over time; only the latest opinion should appear in /recall, full chain in /users/{id}/memories.

messages.content: I love TypeScript, it's my favourite language.
Strong type system has its fans.
TypeScript generics actually annoy me lately, I find them over-engineered.
Generics are tricky.
Settled on TypeScript for big projects, Python for small scripts. That balance works for me.
Pragmatic split.

conversations._purpose: Supersession arc on employer. /recall should report Notion (current); /users/{id}/memories shows Stripe inactive.

messages.content: I work at Stripe as a payments engineer.
Big infrastructure work.
Just started at Notion as a PM this week.
Congrats on the new role.

conversations._purpose: Implicit-fact probe: 'walking Biscuit' implies pet ownership without naming the species directly.

messages.content: Just got back from walking Biscuit in the park. Beautiful morning.
Sounds lovely.

probes.label: multihop-pet-city
probes.query: What city does the user with the dog named Biscuit live in?

probes.label: arc-typescript-current
probes.query: What does the user think of TypeScript?
probes._note: Supersession assertion is deferred to arc-employer probe — the LLM uses variable key namespaces for opinions across turns (opinion.typescript.generics / language.favourite / programming.language), so a key_prefix predicate here is fragile against LLM non-determinism. arc-employer's deterministic key='employment.company' covers the §4.1 chain assertion.

probes.label: arc-employer-current
probes.query: Where does this user currently work?

probes.label: noise-quantum
probes.query: What is the user's opinion on quantum computing?

probes.label: implicit-pet
probes.query: Does this user have any pets?
